title: Filming, recording: One Hand Clapping; Mixing: Junior’s Farm, Sally G by Wings | 1974
content:
Studio Two, EMI Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Geoff Emerick

Wings began work on the One Hand Clapping project on 24 August 1974.

Paul McCartney wanted to rehearse a number of new songs by Wings before they went on the road, and decided to have their rehearsals filmed. He enlisted photographer David Litchfield to direct, and booked at week at Abbey Road, with Geoff Emerick recording the audio.

On this first day, Litchfield set up three cameras on the studio floor and McCartney ran through several songs. He began by performing ‘Sally G’ on an acoustic guitar, before playing ‘Nineteen Hundred And Eighty Five’ at the piano. He then performed versions of ‘Blackbird’, ‘Blackpool’, ‘Country Dreamer’, ‘Twenty Flight Rock’, ‘Peggy Sue’, and ‘I’m Gonna Love You Too’.

The recordings were for Emerick to get the sound right, and for Litchfield’s crew to be positioned correctly. With that complete, McCartney and Emerick mixed ‘Junior’s Farm’ in seven attempts, and ‘Sally G’ in three.
